Over Arctic sea ice, the turbulent sensible heat flux H_\mathrm{S} is commonly estimated with a bulk formula
driven by reanalysis data. Assessing such estimates requires a measured reference. During BACSAM-II (Svalbard,
April 2024), the T-Bird, a sensor package towed about 23 m above the ice below the research aircraft Polar 6,
sampled wind and temperature at 100 Hz, from which the flux is obtained by eddy covariance (EC).

All estimates are evaluated on the same 5 km flight segments:

Symbol

Method

Inputs

H_\mathrm{S,obs,EC}

eddy covariance; the reference against which all other estimates are evaluated

100 Hz w, \theta from the T-Bird

H_\mathrm{S,obs,bulk}

bulk formula

measured: KT-19 surface temperature, T-Bird air temperature, wind and pressure

H_\mathrm{S,RS,bulk}

bulk formula

MODIS surface temperature (ERA5 skin temperature under cloud) and ERA5 air temperature, wind and pressure at the model level closest to the T-Bird

H_\mathrm{S,ERA,bulk}

bulk formula

ERA5 only

H_\mathrm{S,ERA,diag}, H_\mathrm{S,CAR,diag}

model output

surface flux diagnosed by ERA5 and CARRA

From top to bottom, measured inputs are successively replaced by products with pan-Arctic coverage, so that a
loss of skill can be attributed to the replaced input.

The chapters follow the paper’s sections: the EC reference (2), the bulk method (3), the comparison (4), and sensitivity and
uncertainty (5).

Note

All numbers are computed from the files in data/ with the fluxpy functions that produce the paper, and hand
calculations are checked against the pipeline output. Symbols are defined in the 

glossary.
The notebooks can be run in Jupyter from the book/ folder (pixi run jupyter lab).

Paper: Sects. 1–2, Table 1, Fig. 1. Code: scripts/calc_bulk_and_ec_fluxes.py evaluates all six
estimates on the segments and writes data/model_output/sensitivity_figure_data.nc, which this chapter reads.

import sys, warnings
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, xarray as xr
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
REPO = Path("..").resolve(); sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))
plt.rcParams.update({"figure.dpi": 110, "figure.constrained_layout.use": True, "axes.grid": True, "grid.alpha": 0.3, "font.size": 10})

AR  = REPO / "data/observations/ar"
FIG = xr.open_dataset(REPO / "data/model_output/sensitivity_figure_data.nc")      # all flux estimates on the segments
SEG = xr.open_dataset(AR / "analysis_ready_polar6_turbulent_fluxes_latest_5km.nc").sel(start_time=FIG.start_time.values)
EC  = FIG["H_obs_ec"].values

The analysis uses the constant-altitude legs flown over sea ice with the T-Bird below 50 m; within a segment the
T-Bird height varies by less than 30 m (paper Sect. 2.1 and Appendix A1). The low-level legs of 25 April were flown
over open water and are excluded.

t = pd.to_datetime(SEG.start_time.values)
tab = pd.DataFrame({"segments": 1, "T-Bird height (m)": SEG.altitude.values,
                    "EC flux (W m-2)": EC, "KT-19 surface temp. (degC)": SEG.t_kt19.values}, index=t)
g = tab.groupby(tab.index.strftime("%d %B"))
out = g.agg({"segments": "sum", "T-Bird height (m)": "mean", "EC flux (W m-2)": "median", "KT-19 surface temp. (degC)": "mean"}).round(1)
print(f"{len(tab)} segments of 5 km = {5 * len(tab)} km of low-level flight\n"); out





The fluxes are small: over compact sea ice in spring, surface and air temperatures are nearly equal. With fluxes of
a few W m⁻², an estimate of zero everywhere already has a small error. The estimates are therefore assessed by the
amplitude they recover (regression slope) and by their correlation with the reference, not by the RMSE (Chapter 4).

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 2.8))
ax.hist(EC[np.isfinite(EC)], bins=np.arange(-8, 15, 1), color="0.35")
ax.axvline(0, color="k", lw=0.8); ax.set_xlabel("EC sensible heat flux (W m$^{-2}$, positive upward)"); ax.set_ylabel("segments")
print(f"median {np.nanmedian(EC):.1f} W m-2, {np.mean(np.abs(EC[np.isfinite(EC)]) < 2) * 100:.0f} % of the segments within +-2 W m-2")





Figure 1.1. Distribution of the EC sensible heat flux over all segments (bins of 1 W m⁻², positive upward).

Flight tracks (Fig. 1):

Turbulent eddies transport heat upward when rising air (w' > 0) is on average warmer (\theta' > 0) than
sinking air. The sensible heat flux is this covariance multiplied by the heat capacity of air:H_\mathrm{S} = \rho\, c_p\, \overline{w'\theta'}

This chapter derives the flux of one 5 km segment from the 100 Hz data and reproduces the value stored for it in the
segment file data/observations/ar/analysis_ready_polar6_turbulent_fluxes_latest_5km.nc. That file holds one row per
5 km segment (EC flux, random error, integrity check and segment means) and is written by
scripts/run_ec_aggregation.py; its variables are listed under 

Data files.

Note

Paper: Sect. 3.1, Eq. (1), Fig. 3, Appendix A. Code: fluxpy/eddy_covariance.py
(band_covariance, band_covariance_random_error, segment_flux), fluxpy/qc.py (integrity check),
scripts/ec_window_length.py (Fig. 3), scripts/ec_quality.py (every number of Appendix A).

import sys, warnings
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, xarray as xr
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
REPO = Path("..").resolve(); sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))
plt.rcParams.update({"figure.dpi": 110, "figure.constrained_layout.use": True, "axes.grid": True, "grid.alpha": 0.3, "font.size": 10})

AR  = REPO / "data/observations/ar"
FIG = xr.open_dataset(REPO / "data/model_output/sensitivity_figure_data.nc")      # all flux estimates on the segments
SEG = xr.open_dataset(AR / "analysis_ready_polar6_turbulent_fluxes_latest_5km.nc").sel(start_time=FIG.start_time.values)
EC  = FIG["H_obs_ec"].values

from fluxpy.eddy_covariance import band_covariance, segment_flux
from fluxpy.util import CP, RD, add_theta

TB = xr.open_dataset(REPO / "data/observations/processed/t-bird_unified/noseboom_unified.nc").sortby("time")
i = int(np.nanargmax(EC))                                   # the segment with the largest upward flux
t0, t1 = SEG.start_time.values[i], SEG.end_time.values[i]
seg = add_theta(TB.sel(time=slice(t0, t1))).dropna("time", how="any")
print(f"segment {pd.Timestamp(t0):%d %b %Y %H:%M:%S} UTC: {seg.time.size} samples = {seg.time.size / 100:.0f} s at 100 Hz, "
      f"height {float(seg.h.mean()):.0f} m, airspeed {float(seg.tas.mean()):.0f} m/s")

Vertical wind w and potential temperature \theta are measured at 100 Hz. The platform motion has been removed from the wind
with the inertial navigation data; the potential rather than the virtual potential temperature is used because the
air is cold and dry (paper Sect. 3.1). Removing a linear trend from both series yields the fluctuations w' and
\theta'.

from scipy.signal import detrend
w, th = detrend(seg.w.values), detrend(seg.theta.values)
x_km = np.arange(w.size) / 100 * float(seg.tas.mean()) / 1000
fig, axs = plt.subplots(3, 1, figsize=(8, 5), sharex=True)
axs[0].plot(x_km, w, lw=0.4, color="C0"); axs[0].set_ylabel("w' (m s$^{-1}$)")
axs[1].plot(x_km, th, lw=0.4, color="C3"); axs[1].set_ylabel(r"$\theta$' (K)")
axs[2].plot(x_km, np.cumsum(w * th) / w.size, color="k"); axs[2].set_ylabel(r"running sum of w'$\theta$'"); axs[2].set_xlabel("distance along the segment (km)")
print(f"plain covariance of the detrended series: {np.mean(w * th):.4f} K m/s")





Figure 2.1. Detrended vertical wind w' (top) and potential temperature \theta' (middle) along the segment, and
the running sum of w'\theta' divided by the number of samples (bottom), which ends at the covariance of the segment.

The cospectrum distributes the covariance over frequency. At the mean airspeed of 62 m s⁻¹, a frequency f
corresponds to an eddy length of 62\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}/f. The flux is the cospectrum integrated between
0.1 and 20 Hz (eddies of about 3 to 620 m): slower variations are attributed to mesoscale changes along the
track, faster ones to instrument noise. Only the shaded band enters the flux.

n, fs = w.size, 100.0
f = np.fft.rfftfreq(n, 1 / fs)
co = 2 * np.real(np.fft.rfft(w) * np.conj(np.fft.rfft(th))) / n**2       # one-sided cospectrum; sums to the covariance
edges = np.logspace(np.log10(f[1]), np.log10(50), 40); mid = np.sqrt(edges[:-1] * edges[1:])
binned = np.array([co[(f >= a) & (f < b)].sum() for a, b in zip(edges[:-1], edges[1:])])

fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 3.2))
axs[0].bar(mid, binned, width=np.diff(edges), color="0.4"); axs[0].set_xscale("log")
axs[0].set_ylabel("covariance per frequency bin (K m s$^{-1}$)"); axs[0].set_title("cospectrum")
axs[1].plot(f[1:], np.cumsum(co[1:][::-1])[::-1], color="k"); axs[1].set_xscale("log")
axs[1].set_ylabel("covariance from f upwards (K m s$^{-1}$)"); axs[1].set_title("cumulative from high to low frequency")
for ax in axs:
    ax.axvspan(0.1, 20, color="C1", alpha=0.15); ax.set_xlabel("frequency (Hz)")
in_band = band_covariance(w, th, fs, 0.1, 20.0)
print(f"covariance inside 0.1-20 Hz: {in_band:.4f} K m/s = {in_band / np.mean(w * th) * 100:.0f} % of the total covariance of this segment")





Figure 2.2. Left: cospectrum of w' and \theta', summed in logarithmically spaced frequency bins. Right:
covariance contained in all frequencies above f, accumulated from high to low frequency. The shaded band
(0.1–20 Hz) is the part that enters the flux.

rho = float((seg.p * 100 / (RD * (seg["T"] + 273.15))).mean())        # dry-air density from p (hPa) and T (degC)
H_by_hand = rho * CP * in_band
H_fluxpy = segment_flux(seg).flux
print(f"rho = {rho:.2f} kg m-3, c_p = {CP:.0f} J kg-1 K-1")
print(f"H by hand            : {H_by_hand:6.2f} W m-2")
print(f"H from fluxpy        : {float(H_fluxpy):6.2f} W m-2")
print(f"H in the segment file: {float(SEG.sensible_heat_flux[i]):6.2f} W m-2")

Two properties are assessed separately.

Integrity. Resolved turbulence shows the inertial-subrange slope in the power spectrum of w,
|s_w + 5/3| \le 0.4. The slope is reported for every segment; no segment is excluded by it. Table A1 of the paper
repeats the comparison on the segments within tolerances of 0.3 to 0.6.

Precision. A covariance from about 81 s of data carries a random error, because only a finite number of eddies is
sampled. It is estimated from the data (Finkelstein and Sims, 2001). For a true flux of zero, the estimate exceeds
1, 2 and 3 \sigma_\mathrm{rand} by chance in 32 %, 5 % and 0.3 % of cases.

Fluxes that do not exceed their random error are retained. Over compact sea ice a flux indistinguishable from zero
is the typical and physically valid result; discarding such segments would bias the reference towards large fluxes. For
the same reason, criteria formulated as ratios to the flux (such as signal-to-noise ratios) are not applied: they reject
small fluxes and accept large ones irrespective of the quality of the measurement.

from fluxpy.qc import segment_spectra, turbulence_resolved
from fluxpy.eddy_covariance import band_covariance_random_error
slope = segment_spectra(w=seg.w.values, theta=seg.theta.values, u=seg.u.values, v=seg.v.values, fs=100.0)["slope_w"]
sigma = rho * CP * band_covariance_random_error(w, th, fs)
print(f"this segment: spectral slope of w = {slope:.2f} -> turbulence resolved: {turbulence_resolved(slope)}")
print(f"              flux {float(H_fluxpy):.1f} W m-2, random error {sigma:.2f} W m-2 -> {abs(float(H_fluxpy)) / sigma:.0f} sigma")
ratio = FIG.ec_flux_over_sigma.values
print(f"\nall {ratio.size} segments: {int(SEG.turbulence_resolved.sum())} satisfy the integrity check (none is excluded); "
      f"median random error {np.median(FIG.sigma_random_ec.values):.2f} W m-2")
days = pd.to_datetime(FIG.start_time.values).strftime("%d %b")
pd.DataFrame({f"|H| > {k} sigma": {**{d: f"{(ratio[days == d] > k).sum()} / {(days == d).sum()}" for d in pd.unique(days)},
                                   "all": f"{(ratio > k).sum()} / {ratio.size}"} for k in (1, 2, 3)})





On 15 April, the day with open leads and the largest fluxes, all fluxes clearly exceed their random error, and on
23 April most do; on 13 and 17 April most fluxes are statistically indistinguishable from zero. This is a property of
the surface, not a defect of the data, and it limits the correlation attainable by any estimate (Chapter 4).

Short windows under-sample the larger eddies; long windows average over leads and ice. Each of the six low-level legs
is cut into consecutive sub-windows of different length, and their mean flux is compared with the flux of the stretch
they cover, i.e. the leg without the remainder shorter than one window. Where a window edge cuts through a strong flux
event, the ratio depends on where the grid of windows starts; it is therefore averaged over five grid positions, shifted
by a fifth of the window length each (scripts/ec_window_length.py).

wl = pd.read_csv(AR / "ec_leg_length_sensitivity/ec_sensitivity_summary.csv").query("length_km >= 1 and label != 'full leg'")
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 3))
axs[0].errorbar(wl.length_km, wl.ratio_mean, wl.ratio_std, fmt="o-", color="C1", ecolor="0.5", capsize=2)
axs[0].axhline(1, color="k", ls="--"); axs[0].set_ylabel("sub-window flux / stretch flux")
axs[1].plot(wl.length_km, wl.random_error_median, "s-", color="C4"); axs[1].set_ylabel("random error (W m$^{-2}$)")
for ax in axs:
    ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.axvline(5, color="goldenrod", lw=3, ls="--"); ax.set_xlabel("window length (km)")
r5 = wl[wl.length_km == 5].iloc[0]
print(f"at 5 km: flux ratio {r5.ratio_mean:.2f}, random error {r5.random_error_median:.2f} W m-2, fluxes above 2 sigma {r5.fraction_above_2sigma * 100:.0f} %")





Figure 2.3. Left: mean flux of the sub-windows of a leg relative to the flux of the stretch they cover, averaged
over five grid positions, as a function of the window length (mean and standard deviation over the legs with a flux of
at least 0.5 W m^{-2}). Right: median random error of the sub-window fluxes. The
dashed line marks the 5 km segments of the analysis.

The total uncertainty combines, in quadrature, the random error (above) and the instrument error (5 %, from the
flow calibration of the five-hole probe). The placement spread, obtained by shifting the 5 km window along the leg in
0.05 km steps (scripts/ec_segment_placement.py), is an independent, empirical estimate of the random error. It is
reported as a cross-check and not added.

from fluxpy.uncertainty import uncertainty_budget
U = uncertainty_budget(FIG)
pd.DataFrame({k.replace("ec_", ""): [np.nanmedian(U[k]), np.nanpercentile(U[k], 25), np.nanpercentile(U[k], 75)]
              for k in ("ec_random", "ec_instrument", "ec_total", "ec_placement")},
             index=["median (W m-2)", "25th percentile", "75th percentile"]).round(2)



Appendix A of the paper contains two further checks, printed by pixi run ec-quality: the comparison is insensitive to
the screening of the fluxes (Table A1, eight alternative screenings), and the pitch resonance of the towed T-Bird near
1 Hz reduces the larger fluxes by less than a tenth (median), with practically no effect on the comparison.

Summary. The reference flux is a band-limited covariance that can be recomputed from the 100 Hz data in a few lines.
Its uncertainty is dominated by the finite number of eddies in 5 km, as confirmed by the placement spread, not by the
instrument.

Without turbulence measurements, the flux is estimated from mean quantities:H_\mathrm{S} = \rho\, c_p\, C_\mathrm{h}\, U\, (\theta_\mathrm{s} - \theta_\mathrm{air})

the wind speed U times the surface–air temperature difference, scaled by the transfer coefficient
C_\mathrm{h}, which describes the efficiency of turbulent mixing. C_\mathrm{h} depends on

the roughness of the surface: z_{0,m} for momentum and z_{0,T} = \alpha_T\, z_{0,m} for heat;

the stability, expressed by the bulk Richardson number Ri_\mathrm{b}: stable stratification
(Ri_\mathrm{b} > 0, surface colder than the air) suppresses turbulence, unstable stratification enhances it.

This chapter computes H_\mathrm{S,obs,bulk} for one segment and shows the dependence of C_\mathrm{h} on stability
and on \alpha_T.

Note

Paper: Sect. 3.2, Eq. (2), Appendix B, Table B1. Code: fluxpy/bulk.py (steps B1–B3),
fluxpy/stability.py (Eq. B3), fluxpy/stability_lib.py (the eight stability schemes), fluxpy/util.py
(constants, potential temperature, pressures).

import sys, warnings
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, xarray as xr
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
REPO = Path("..").resolve(); sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))
plt.rcParams.update({"figure.dpi": 110, "figure.constrained_layout.use": True, "axes.grid": True, "grid.alpha": 0.3, "font.size": 10})

AR  = REPO / "data/observations/ar"
FIG = xr.open_dataset(REPO / "data/model_output/sensitivity_figure_data.nc")      # all flux estimates on the segments
SEG = xr.open_dataset(AR / "analysis_ready_polar6_turbulent_fluxes_latest_5km.nc").sel(start_time=FIG.start_time.values)
EC  = FIG["H_obs_ec"].values

from fluxpy.util import potential_temperature, air_density, CP, G
from fluxpy.stability import bulk_richardson_2pt, Cd_Ch_noniterative
from fluxpy.bulk import reference_config
cfg = reference_config()
i = int(np.nanargmax(EC)); s = SEG.isel(start_time=i)
print("reference configuration:", cfg.scheme_name, "| alpha_T =", cfg.zt_ratio, "| z0 (open/thin/thick) =", cfg.z0_ocean, cfg.z0_thin_ice, cfg.z0_thick_ice, "m")

The surface temperature is taken from the KT-19 infrared pyrometer, air temperature and wind from the T-Bird, all
averaged over the 5 km segment. Both temperatures are converted to potential temperature with the pressure at their
own height. Pressure is measured at the T-Bird, about 23 m above the ice, not at the surface; the surface pressure
follows from the hypsometric equation,p_\mathrm{s} = p_z \exp\!\left(\frac{g\,z}{R_d\,\bar T}\right),

about 3 hPa above the T-Bird value. Using p_z at the surface would make \theta_\mathrm{s} too warm by
g z / c_p \approx 0.23 K, which is not negligible against typical temperature differences of one to two kelvin. The
reanalysis-driven estimates apply the same rule: the ERA5 surface pressure for \theta_\mathrm{s}, and the pressure of
model level 136 (about 31 m; fluxpy.util.era5_level_pressure) for the air temperature of that level.

from fluxpy.util import surface_pressure_hypsometric
T_s, T_a, p, z = float(s.t_kt19), float(s.T_mean), float(s.p_mean), float(s.altitude)
u, v = float(s.u_mean), float(s.v_mean); U = np.hypot(u, v)
p_s = float(surface_pressure_hypsometric(p, z, T_mean=0.5 * (T_s + T_a)))
th_s, th_a = float(potential_temperature(T_s, p_s)), float(potential_temperature(T_a, p))
print(f"pressure {p:.1f} hPa at the T-Bird ({z:.0f} m)  ->  {p_s:.1f} hPa at the surface")
print(f"surface {T_s:.1f} degC, air {T_a:.1f} degC  ->  theta_s - theta_air = {th_s - th_a:+.2f} K "
      f"(with the T-Bird pressure at the surface it would be {float(potential_temperature(T_s, p)) - th_a:+.2f} K);  wind {U:.1f} m/s")

Ri_\mathrm{b} = \frac{g}{\bar\theta}\,\frac{\Delta\theta\,\Delta z}{\Delta u^2 + \Delta v^2}

between the surface (zero wind) and the measurement height; negative values indicate unstable stratification.

Ri = float(bulk_richardson_2pt(dtheta=th_a - th_s, dz=z, du=u, dv=v, theta_ref=0.5 * (th_s + th_a), eps_wind2=cfg.ri_eps_wind2))
print(f"Ri_b = {Ri:+.2f}  ->", "unstable (surface warmer than air)" if Ri < 0 else "stable")

Within 5 km the surface consists of open water, thin ice and snow-covered ice. Each KT-19 sample is classified by its
temperature (above −1.8 °C: open water; at or below −20 °C: snow-covered ice; in between: thin ice). The effective
roughness length is the logarithmic average over the three fractions.

fr = np.array([float(s.frac_open), float(s.frac_thin_ice), float(s.frac_thick_ice)])
z0 = float(np.exp(fr @ np.log([cfg.z0_ocean, cfg.z0_thin_ice, cfg.z0_thick_ice]))); zT = cfg.zt_ratio * z0
print(f"fractions open / thin / snow-covered: {fr.round(2)}  ->  z0m = {z0:.1e} m,  z0T = alpha_T * z0m = {zT:.1e} m")

Cd, Ch = Cd_Ch_noniterative(Ri, z, z0, zT, cfg.scheme_name)
_, Ch_neutral = Cd_Ch_noniterative(0.0, z, z0, zT, cfg.scheme_name)
rho = float(air_density(T_a, p))
H = rho * CP * Ch * U * (th_s - th_a)
print(f"C_h = {Ch:.2e}  (neutral value {Ch_neutral:.2e}: stability changes it by a factor {Ch / Ch_neutral:.2f})")
print(f"H bulk by hand      : {H:6.1f} W m-2")
print(f"H bulk from pipeline: {float(FIG.H_obs_bulk[i]):6.1f} W m-2")
print(f"H measured (EC)     : {EC[i]:6.1f} W m-2")

The stability dependence follows from Monin–Obukhov similarity theory, for which several formulations exist. The paper
uses Gryanik et al. (2020, GLGS20) as reference and tests seven alternatives. The shading marks the range of
Ri_\mathrm{b} sampled during the campaign (central 90 % of the segments). All schemes share the unstable branch; on
the stable branch they differ, but there C_\mathrm{h} and the flux are small in every scheme. The effect on the
comparison is quantified in Chapter 5.

lo, hi = np.nanpercentile(FIG.Ri_obs.values, [5, 95])                 # central 90 % of the sampled Ri_b
ri = np.linspace(min(-1.0, lo), max(0.5, hi), 300)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 3.4))
for name in ["GLGS20", "BD", "HB88", "BH91", "CB05", "GAFGP07"]:
    ax.plot(ri, [Cd_Ch_noniterative(r, 24.0, 3e-4, 3e-5, name)[1] * 1e3 for r in ri], label=name, lw=2 if name == "GLGS20" else 1)
ax.axvspan(lo, hi, color="0.85")
ax.axvline(0, color="k", lw=0.6); ax.set_xlabel("bulk Richardson number"); ax.set_ylabel("$C_h$ × 10$^3$"); ax.legend(ncol=2, fontsize=8)
ax.set_title("z = 24 m, z$_{0m}$ = 3·10$^{-4}$ m, α$_T$ = 0.1");



Figure 3.1. Transfer coefficient C_\mathrm{h} as a function of the bulk Richardson number for six of the eight
stability schemes, at the height and roughness given in the title. The grey band is the range of Ri_\mathrm{b} sampled
during the campaign.

The scalar roughness ratio \alpha_T = z_{0,T}/z_{0,m} is poorly constrained over sea ice: models use values between 1
(ERA5) and 0.1 (large-eddy simulations; the reference of the paper), whereas theory and earlier aircraft measurements
indicate much smaller values. C_\mathrm{h} depends on it logarithmically:

a = np.logspace(-7, 0, 50)
ch = np.array([Cd_Ch_noniterative(0.0, 24.0, 3e-4, 3e-4 * x, "GLGS20")[1] for x in a])
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3)); ax.semilogx(a, ch / ch[np.argmin(abs(a - 0.1))], color="k")
ax.axvline(0.1, color="C2", ls="--"); ax.axvline(1e-2, color="C1", ls="--")
ax.set_xlabel(r"$\alpha_T$"); ax.set_ylabel(r"$C_h$ relative to $\alpha_T$ = 0.1")
print(f"alpha_T from 1e-1 to 1e-4 (three orders of magnitude) changes C_h by a factor {ch[np.argmin(abs(a - 1e-4))] / ch[np.argmin(abs(a - 0.1))]:.2f}")





Figure 3.2. C_\mathrm{h} under neutral stratification as a function of \alpha_T, relative to its value at
\alpha_T = 0.1. Dashed lines: reference configuration (\alpha_T = 0.1, green) and amplitude-matched configuration
(\alpha_T = 10^{-2}, orange).

Summary. The bulk flux is the product of wind speed, temperature difference and C_\mathrm{h}, which contains
roughness and stability. Roughness scales the flux and thus changes its amplitude, but not where along the track the
flux is large or small; that is determined by the temperature difference and the wind. This distinction structures the
results of Chapters 4 and 5.

Most measured fluxes lie within a few W m⁻² of zero (Chapter 1), so an estimate close to zero everywhere has a small
error without containing information. The table therefore includes the trivial estimate H = 0 on every segment; its
mean absolute error (MAE) and RMSE can be compared with those of the actual estimates.

The paper uses two separate measures:

slope b of the regression of the estimate on the EC flux: the fraction of the observed amplitude recovered (ideal: 1);

correlation r: agreement of estimate and reference in their variability (ideal: 1).

The slope equals r times the ratio of the standard deviations of estimate and reference. A slope near 1 can therefore
result from the correct amplitude with good correlation or from excess variance with poor correlation; b and r are
interpreted together.

    Parameters
    ----------
    legs         : T-Bird 100 Hz time slices, one per leg (``T`` degC, ``p`` hPa,

    ds_kt19 : KT-19 surface temperature [degC] (50 Hz, PANGAEA 995980; scripts/prepare_inputs.py).

    -------

    """
    rows: list[dict] = []
    n_evaluated = 0

    for leg in tqdm(legs, desc="legs"):
        if leg.time.size == 0:
            continue
        leg = _add_along_track_distance(add_theta(leg))
        leg_length_km = float(leg.distance[-1] - leg.distance[0])

        for left_km, right_km in _segment_edges(leg_length_km, cfg.length_km):
            n_evaluated += 1
            segment = leg.sel(distance=slice(left_km, right_km)).dropna("distance", how="any", subset=_REQUIRED)
            n_samples = int(segment.distance.size)
            if n_samples < cfg.min_samples:
                if cfg.verbose:
                    print(f"  skipped [{left_km:.0f}, {right_km:.0f}] km: {n_samples} samples")
                continue
            height_range = float(segment["h"].max() - segment["h"].min())
            if height_range > cfg.max_height_range_m:
                if cfg.verbose:
                    print(f"  skipped [{left_km:.0f}, {right_km:.0f}] km: height varies by {height_range:.0f} m")
                continue

            start = pd.to_datetime(segment["time"][0].item())
            end = pd.to_datetime(segment["time"][-1].item())

            # -- EC flux, random error, integrity check (Sect. 3.1, Appendix A) --
            ec = segment_flux(segment, fs=cfg.fs)
            spectra = segment_spectra(segment["w"].values, segment["theta"].values,
                                      segment["u"].values, segment["v"].values, fs=cfg.fs)
            resolved = turbulence_resolved(spectra["slope_w"])

            # -- surface: KT-19, sea-ice concentration -----------------------------
            kt19 = ds_kt19[cfg.kt19_var].sel(time=slice(start, end))
            composition = _surface_composition(kt19.values.astype(float), cfg)

            rows.append({
                "start_time": start,
                "end_time": end,
                "N_samples": n_samples,
                "segment_length_km": float(right_km - left_km),
                # T-Bird segment means (inputs of the T-Bird bulk estimate)
                "altitude": float(segment["h"].mean()),
                "T_mean": float(segment["T"].mean()),
                "p_mean": float(segment["p"].mean()),
                "u_mean": float(segment["u"].mean()),
                "v_mean": float(segment["v"].mean()),
                "latitude": float(segment["lat"].mean()),
                "longitude": float(segment["lon"].mean()),
                # EC reference

                "sensible_heat_flux_random_error": ec.random_error,
                "flux_over_random_error": ec.flux_over_random_error,
                "qc_slope_w": spectra["slope_w"],
                "turbulence_resolved": float(resolved),

    r"""Effective roughness lengths of each segment from its surface fractions (Eq. B4),

    $$ \ln z_{0,m}^\mathrm{eff} = \sum_i f_i \ln z_{0,m,i}, \qquad
       z_{0,T}^\mathrm{eff} = \alpha_T z_{0,m}^\mathrm{eff}, $$

    i.e. a fraction-weighted geometric mean over open water, thin ice and
    snow-covered ice. The logarithm is the right average because z0 enters the
    transfer coefficient through ln(z/z0). Fractions are clipped to [0, 1] and
    renormalised; segments without valid fractions get NaN.

    f = np.clip(np.where(np.isfinite(f), f, 0.0), 0.0, 1.0)
    total = f.sum(axis=1)

    ln_z0 = np.full(f.shape[0], np.nan)
    ln_z0[valid] = (f[valid] / total[valid, None]) @ np.log([cfg.z0_ocean, cfg.z0_thin_ice, cfg.z0_thick_ice])
    z0 = np.exp(ln_z0)
    return z0, z0 * cfg.zt_ratio

Source code (fluxpy/eddy_covariance.py, lines 56–80)def band_covariance(x: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, fs: float,
                    fmin: float = FLUX_BAND_HZ[0], fmax: float = FLUX_BAND_HZ[1]) -> float:
    """Covariance of ``x`` and ``y`` carried by frequencies ``fmin <= f <= fmax``.

    The one-sided cospectrum of the full record (no segmenting, no taper) is
    summed over the band. By Parseval's theorem the sum over ALL frequencies
    equals the ordinary covariance ``mean(x' y')``; the result is therefore
    exactly the in-band part of the covariance. The frequency resolution is
    ``fs / n`` (about 0.012 Hz for a 5 km segment), so the band edges are met
    to within one such bin. ``x`` and ``y`` must be detrended 1-D arrays of
    equal length.
    """
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    n = x.size
    X = np.fft.rfft(x - x.mean())
    Y = np.fft.rfft(y - y.mean())
    cospectrum = np.real(X * np.conj(Y)) / float(n) ** 2     # two-sided, per bin
    one_sided = np.full(cospectrum.size, 2.0)                # fold negative frequencies ...
    one_sided[0] = 1.0                                       # ... except the mean
    if n % 2 == 0:
        one_sided[-1] = 1.0                                  # ... and the Nyquist bin
    f = np.fft.rfftfreq(n, d=1.0 / fs)
    in_band = (f >= fmin) & (f <= fmax)
    return float(np.dot(one_sided[in_band], cospectrum[in_band]))

    r"""Random (sampling) error of the band-limited covariance, 1 sigma.

    Finkelstein and Sims (2001, J. Geophys. Res. 106, 3503-3509), Eq. (8)-(10):
    the variance of a covariance estimated from ``n`` samples is

        $$ \sigma^2 = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{p=-m}^{m} \left[ \gamma_{xx}(p)\, \gamma_{yy}(p)
           + \gamma_{xy}(p)\, \gamma_{yx}(p) \right] $$

    with the auto- and cross-covariance functions gamma at lag ``p``. They are
    evaluated on the series band-passed to ``[fmin, fmax]`` so that the error
    belongs to the same quantity as :func:`band_covariance`. ``m`` covers
    ``max_lag_s`` seconds, several times the integral time scale; the result
    changes by a few per cent for 5 to 30 s (Rannik et al., 2016, found the
    estimator robust and insensitive to this choice).

    Note: the often quoted shortcut ``sqrt(2 L / X)`` (Lenschow et al., 1994)
    lacks the factor ``sqrt((1 + r^2) / r^2)`` of the correlation ``r`` between
    ``x`` and ``y``; for the weakly correlated w and theta over sea ice
    (|r| ~ 0.08) it understates the error by an order of magnitude.
    """
    xb = band_pass(x, fs, fmin, fmax)
    yb = band_pass(y, fs, fmin, fmax)
    n = xb.size

    def covariance_function(a, b):
        """Circular (FFT) covariance function g_ab(p), normalised by n."""
        return np.fft.irfft(np.fft.rfft(a) * np.conj(np.fft.rfft(b)), n=n) / n

    m = int(max_lag_s * fs)
    lags = np.r_[0:m + 1, n - m:n]                          # p = 0..m and p = -m..-1
    var = (covariance_function(xb, xb)[lags] * covariance_function(yb, yb)[lags]
           + covariance_function(xb, yb)[lags] * covariance_function(yb, xb)[lags]).sum() / n
    return float(np.sqrt(max(var, 0.0)))

                    fs: float) -> dict:
    """Spectra of one segment as shown in Fig. A1, plus the integrity-check slope.

    Parameters
    ----------
    w, theta, u, v : 100 Hz series of the segment (raw; detrended here).
    fs             : sampling frequency [Hz].

    Returns
    -------
    dict with
    ``f``                  Welch frequency axis [Hz]
    ``P_theta``, ``P_w``, ``P_u``, ``P_v``   one-sided power spectra (Fig. A1a-d)
    ``f_cospectrum``       f * Co_w,theta, the frequency-weighted cospectrum (Fig. A1e)
    ``f_fft``, ``ogive_norm``   frequency axis and normalised ogive of the full-record
                           FFT cospectrum (Fig. A1f); resolves down to 1/T_segment
    ``slope_w``            inertial-subrange slope of P_w (Appendix A1)
    ``r2_cumulative_covariance``   R^2 of a straight line through the cumulative
                           covariance along the segment; one of the relative
                           criteria evaluated, and not applied, in Appendix A3
    """
    w = detrend(np.asarray(w, dtype=float), type="linear")
    theta = detrend(np.asarray(theta, dtype=float), type="linear")
    u = detrend(np.asarray(u, dtype=float), type="linear")
    v = detrend(np.asarray(v, dtype=float), type="linear")

    # power spectra and Welch cospectrum (Fig. A1a-e)
    f, P_theta = _welch_spectrum(theta, fs)
    _, P_w = _welch_spectrum(w, fs)
    _, P_u = _welch_spectrum(u, fs)
    _, P_v = _welch_spectrum(v, fs)
    _, cospectrum = _welch_cospectrum(w, theta, fs)

    # full-record FFT cospectrum and its ogive (Fig. A1f): Hann taper, zero-padded
    # to the next power of two, normalised so that Og(0) = 1
    n = w.size
    n_fft = int(2 ** np.ceil(np.log2(n)))
    taper = np.hanning(n)
    taper /= np.sqrt(np.mean(taper ** 2))                    # keep the RMS amplitude
    W = np.fft.rfft(w * taper, n=n_fft)
    TH = np.fft.rfft(theta * taper, n=n_fft)
    f_fft = np.fft.rfftfreq(n_fft, d=1.0 / fs)
    co_fft = np.real(W * np.conj(TH)) / (n_fft * fs)
    co_fft[1:-1] *= 2.0                                      # two-sided -> one-sided
    ogive = _ogive(f_fft, co_fft)
    ogive_norm = ogive / ogive[0] if abs(ogive[0]) > 1e-12 else ogive * np.nan

    # cumulative covariance along the segment vs a straight line (Appendix A3)
    cum_cov = np.cumsum((w - w.mean()) * (theta - theta.mean()))
    cum_cov_norm = cum_cov / cum_cov[-1] if cum_cov[-1] != 0 else cum_cov * np.nan
    fraction = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, n)
    residual = cum_cov_norm - np.polyval(np.polyfit(fraction, cum_cov_norm, 1), fraction)
    ss_tot = float(np.sum((cum_cov_norm - cum_cov_norm.mean()) ** 2))
    r2 = 1.0 - float(np.sum(residual ** 2)) / ss_tot if ss_tot > 0 else np.nan

    return dict(
        f=f, P_theta=P_theta, P_w=P_w, P_u=P_u, P_v=P_v,
        f_cospectrum=f * cospectrum,
        f_fft=f_fft, ogive_norm=ogive_norm,
        slope_w=spectral_slope(f, P_w),
        r2_cumulative_covariance=r2,
    )

    """Amplitude of an estimate ``y`` relative to the EC reference ``x``:
    ordinary-least-squares ``slope`` of y on x (the paper's amplitude metric),
    ``intercept``, and ``std_ratio`` = sigma_y / sigma_x."""
    sxx = float(np.var(x, ddof=1))
    syy = float(np.var(y, ddof=1))
    sxy = float(np.cov(x, y, ddof=1)[0, 1])
    if sxx <= 0 or sxy == 0.0:
        return {"slope": np.nan, "intercept": np.nan, "std_ratio": np.nan}

    return {"slope": float(slope), "intercept": float(np.mean(y) - slope * np.mean(x)),
            "std_ratio": float(np.sqrt(syy / sxx))}

    stable = ok & (dtheta >= 0)                                   # Jordan et al. (1999)
    S[stable] = U[stable] + 0.5 / np.cosh(U[stable])

Source code (fluxpy/stability_lib.py, lines 237–259)def zeta_noniterative(Ri_b: float, eps_m: float, eps_t: float, scheme_name: str) -> float:
    """Stability parameter zeta = z/L from Ri_b without iteration, Eq. (22a-c); stable branch only."""
    if Ri_b <= 0.0:
        return 0.0
    if scheme_name not in SCHEMES:
        raise KeyError(f"Unknown scheme '{scheme_name}'")
    s = SCHEMES[scheme_name]
    ln_em, ln_et = math.log(eps_m), math.log(eps_t)

    # equivalent bulk Richardson number, Eq. (22c)
    hat_Ri = (Ri_b / s.Pr0) * ((1.0 - 1.0 / eps_t) / ((1.0 - 1.0 / eps_m) ** 2))
    # psi_ka, Eq. (22b); the paper uses eps_t for both k = m, h
    psi_ma = s.psi_m(s.zeta_a) - s.psi_m(s.zeta_a / eps_t)
    psi_ha = s.psi_h(s.zeta_a) - s.psi_h(s.zeta_a / eps_t)

    term1 = (ln_em ** 2 / ln_et) * hat_Ri                                 # linear term
    num = (ln_em - psi_ma) ** (2.0 * (s.gamma - 1.0))
    den = (s.zeta_a ** (s.gamma - 1.0)) * ((ln_et - psi_ha / s.Pr0) ** (s.gamma - 1.0))
    if den == 0.0:
        return _clip_stable(term1)
    bracket = ((ln_em - psi_ma) ** 2) / (ln_et - psi_ha / s.Pr0) - (ln_em ** 2) / ln_et
    term2 = (num / den) * bracket * (hat_Ri ** s.gamma)                  # nonlinear term
    return _clip_stable(term1 + term2)

                   max_iter: int = 80, tol: float = 1e-6) -> float:
    """Stability parameter zeta from Ri_b by Newton iteration of the exact relation, Eq. (20).

    Used for the unstable branch (Businger-Dyer psi functions) and as the exact
    reference for the non-iterative stable formula. zeta is kept within
    [ZETA_MIN_UNSTABLE, 50] (unstable) or >= 0 (stable).
    """
    if Ri_b == 0.0:
        return 0.0
    s = _scheme_for(Ri_b, scheme_name)
    ln_em, ln_et = math.log(eps_m), math.log(eps_t)

    if Ri_b > 0.0:
        zeta = zeta_noniterative(Ri_b, eps_m, eps_t, scheme_name) or 0.05
        clip = _clip_stable
    else:
        zeta = max(-0.5, -0.1 * abs(Ri_b))
        clip = lambda z: min(max(z, ZETA_MIN_UNSTABLE), 50.0) if math.isfinite(z) else 0.0   # noqa: E731

    pref = ((1.0 - 1.0 / eps_m) ** 2) / (1.0 - 1.0 / eps_t)

    def residual(z: float) -> float | None:
        num = pref * z * (s.Pr0 * ln_et - s.psi_h(z) + s.psi_h(z / eps_t))
        den = (ln_em - s.psi_m(z) + s.psi_m(z / eps_m)) ** 2
        return None if den == 0.0 else num / den - Ri_b

    for _ in range(max_iter):
        f = residual(zeta)
        if f is None or abs(f) < tol:
            break
        dz = 1e-4 * max(1.0, zeta)
        f2 = residual(zeta + dz)
        if f2 is None:
            break
        df = (f2 - f) / dz
        if df == 0.0 or not math.isfinite(df):
            break
        zeta_new = clip(zeta - f / df)
        if abs(zeta_new - zeta) < tol:
            zeta = zeta_new
            break
        zeta = zeta_new
    return clip(zeta)

Each low-level T-Bird leg is cut into consecutive sub-windows of length L

from matplotlib.patches import Rectangle
from cartopy import crs as ccrs
import cartopy.feature as cfeature
from cmocean import cm as cmo
from cmcrameri import cm as cmc

TRACK_DIR = REPO / "data" / "observations" / "raw" / "polar6" / "mastertracks"
SIC_FP = (REPO / "data" / "observations" / "processed" / "satellite_unified"
          / "sic_modis-aqua_amsr2-gcom-w1_merged_nh_1000m_APRIL.nc")
AR_FP = (REPO / "data" / "observations" / "ar"
         / "analysis_ready_polar6_turbulent_fluxes_latest_5km.nc")

LONGYEARBYEN = (15.63, 78.22)
PC = ccrs.PlateCarree()
HALO = [pe.withStroke(linewidth=1.8, foreground="white")]


def read_mastertrack(fp: Path) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Parse a PANGAEA mastertrack .tab file (skip the /* ... */ header)."""
    txt = fp.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    df = pd.read_csv(StringIO(txt[txt.find("*/") + 2:]), sep="\t")
    df.columns = ["time", "lat", "lon", "alt"]
    df["time"] = pd.to_datetime(df["time"])
    return df


# -- analysed low-level days, batlow day colours, focus regions --------------
low = xr.open_dataset(AR_FP).pipe(lambda d: d.where(d.altitude <= 50, drop=True))
seg_times = pd.to_datetime(low.start_time.values)
low_alt_days = np.unique(seg_times.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"))
day_color = dict(zip(low_alt_days, cmc.batlow(np.linspace(0, 1, len(low_alt_days)))))
# 17 April: batlow's mid-range olive vanished next to the 23-April tracks
# (co-author round 3) -> a saturated red, drawn above the 23-April tracks.
# Keep in sync with the frame colours of fig04_flux_maps.py.
DAY_COLOR_0417 = "#d7191c"
day_color["2024-04-17"] = DAY_COLOR_0417
DAY_ZORDER = {"2024-04-17": 1}        # extra zorder: 17 April on top
analysed_days = [d for d in low_alt_days if d != "2024-04-25"]

# focus regions of the detail panels (a)-(d) of fig04_flux_maps.py
focus = {}
for panel, day in zip("abcd", analysed_days):
    ds_day = low.sel(start_time=day)
    x, y = ds_day.longitude.values, ds_day.latitude.values
    focus[f"({panel})"] = (day, [np.nanmin(x) - 1.0, np.nanmax(x) + 1.0,
                                 np.nanmin(y) - 0.12, np.nanmax(y) + 0.12])

# -- master tracks: coloured if they overlap the analysed segments -----------
tracks = []
for fp in sorted(TRACK_DIR.glob("*_mastertrack.tab")):
    df = read_mastertrack(fp)
    day = df["time"].dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d").iloc[0]
    if day in low_alt_days:
        overlaps = True
    else:
        overlaps = False
    tracks.append((df, day, overlaps and day in analysed_days))

# -- April-mean SIC backdrop (25 April excluded: bad data, 100 % everywhere) -
sic = (xr.open_dataset(SIC_FP).squeeze().sortby("time")
       .drop_sel(time="2024-04-25").sic.mean("time"))

# -- figure ------------------------------------------------------------------
fig, ax = fs.figure(width=fs.COL_W, aspect=0.9,
                    subplot_kw={"projection": ccrs.NorthPolarStereo(
                        central_longitude=LONGYEARBYEN[0])})
lat_north = max(86.0, max(df.lat.max() for df, *_ in tracks) + 0.4)
ax.set_extent([-20, 25, 74, lat_north], crs=PC)

im = ax.contourf(sic.lon, sic.lat, sic, transform=PC, cmap=cmo.ice,
                 levels=np.arange(0, 110, 10), alpha=0.6, rasterized=True)
ax.add_feature(cfeature.LAND, facecolor="lightgray", zorder=1)
ax.add_feature(cfeature.COASTLINE, linewidth=0.5, zorder=2)

# graticule as labelled contours of 2-D lat/lon fields (74\N{DEGREE SIGN}N and
# 0\N{DEGREE SIGN} are drawn but not labelled -- their labels clip at the frame)
glon, glat = np.meshgrid(np.linspace(-40, 45, 341), np.linspace(70, 88, 181))
for field, levels, labelled, fmt in [
        (glat, np.arange(72, 86, 2), np.arange(76, 86, 2),
         lambda v: f"{v:.0f}\N{DEGREE SIGN}N"),
        (glon, np.arange(-30, 45, 10), [-30, -20, -10, 10, 20, 30, 40],
         lambda v: f"{abs(v):.0f}\N{DEGREE SIGN}{'E' if v >= 0 else 'W'}")]:
    cs = ax.contour(glon, glat, field, levels=levels, colors="grey",
                    linewidths=0.4, linestyles=":", transform=PC, zorder=3)
    ax.clabel(cs, levels=[v for v in labelled if v in cs.levels], fmt=fmt,
              fontsize=fs.FONT_SIZE - 1, inline=True)

# flight tracks: grey for all, day colours for the analysed flights; the grey
# tracks are dark with a white outline, so that they stay visible over the light
# grey land and the dark open ocean alike
OTHER_TRACK = dict(color="0.3", linewidth=0.8,
                   path_effects=[pe.withStroke(linewidth=1.6, foreground="white")])
for df, day, analysed in tracks:
    if analysed:
        ax.plot(df.lon, df.lat, color=day_color[day], linewidth=1,
                transform=PC, zorder=6 + 0.5 * DAY_ZORDER.get(day, 0),
                path_effects=[pe.withStroke(linewidth=1.1, foreground="white")])
    else:
        ax.plot(df.lon, df.lat, **OTHER_TRACK, transform=PC, zorder=4)

# focus-region rectangles; (c) and (d) almost coincide, so their labels sit at
# opposite corners of the shared box (d: north-west, c: south-east), each tied
# to its corner by a short leader line; (b) sits below its box, inside the map
# frame (above it, it was cut by the frame)
pc_data = PC._as_mpl_transform(ax)
LABEL_POS = {   # (anchor corner of the box, label offset in points, ha, va)
    "(a)": ("top-left", (-3, 0), "right", "top"),
    "(b)": ("bottom-centre", (0, -3), "center", "top"),
    "(c)": ("bottom-right", (6, -5), "left", "top"),
    "(d)": ("top-left", (-7, 6), "right", "bottom"),
}
for name, (day, (x0, x1, y0, y1)) in focus.items():
    ax.add_patch(Rectangle((x0, y0), x1 - x0, y1 - y0, fill=False,
                           linewidth=.75, edgecolor=day_color[day],
                           transform=PC, zorder=7 + 0.5 * DAY_ZORDER.get(day, 0),
                           alpha=.7, linestyle="--"))
    corner, offset, ha, va = LABEL_POS[name]
    xy = {"top-left": (x0, y1), "bottom-right": (x1, y0),
          "bottom-centre": (0.5 * (x0 + x1), y0)}[corner]
    leader = (dict(arrowstyle="-", color=day_color[day], lw=0.6, shrinkA=0, shrinkB=0)
              if name in ("(c)", "(d)") else None)
    ax.annotate(name, xy=xy, xycoords=pc_data, xytext=offset,
                textcoords="offset points", color=day_color[day], weight="bold",
                ha=ha, va=va, zorder=8, path_effects=HALO, arrowprops=leader)

# geographical references
ax.plot(*LONGYEARBYEN, marker="*", markersize=9, color="k",
        transform=PC, zorder=7)
ax.text(LONGYEARBYEN[0] + 1.1, LONGYEARBYEN[1] - 0.72, "LYR",
        fontsize=fs.FONT_SIZE - 1, transform=PC, zorder=8, path_effects=HALO)
for name, lon, lat, col in [("Svalbard", 19.0, 78.9, "dimgrey"),
                            ("Greenland", -19.0, 80.3, "dimgrey"),
                            ("Fram Strait", -4.0, 79.3, "black"),
                            ("Arctic Ocean", 2.0, 85.0, "black")]:
    ax.text(lon, lat, name, fontsize=fs.FONT_SIZE - 1, color=col,
            style="italic", ha="center", va="center", transform=PC, zorder=7,
            path_effects=HALO)

# legend and colourbar
handles = [Line2D([0], [0], color=day_color[d], linewidth=1.8,
                  label=pd.Timestamp(d).strftime("%d %B"))
           for d in analysed_days]
handles.append(Line2D([0], [0], **OTHER_TRACK, label="Other flights"))
ax.legend(handles=handles, loc="lower left", frameon=True, framealpha=0.9,
          title="Flight tracks")

cbar = fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, fraction=0.035, pad=0.02)
cbar.set_label("Sea-ice concentration (%)")

ax.spines["geo"].set_visible(False)

fs.save(fig, "fig01_campaign_overview")

For the 91 segments of the four low-level flight days:
(a) pseudo profiles of potential temperature per flight day: the surface value
    theta_s and theta_air at the T-Bird (~23 m) and Polar 6 (~73 m) levels for the
    observations, and the corresponding levels of ERA5 (with ERA5 or MODIS T_s) and

Inputs (all shipped): the segment file (KT-19 T_s, T-Bird T, p, height), the Polar 6
aircraft-level side file, MODIS IST, ERA5 model levels 134-137 and single levels,
CARRA surface and 30 / 75 m height levels. MODIS and ERA5 are colocated with the
same functions as the bulk fluxes (scripts/calc_bulk_and_ec_fluxes.py); the
potential temperature is fluxpy.util.potential_temperature with the pressure of
each level.

Run:  pixi run python figures_manuscript/fig02_meteo_overview.py
"""
import logging
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "scripts"))
logging.getLogger("fontTools").setLevel(logging.WARNING)

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import xarray as xr
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

from fluxpy import figstyle as fs
from fluxpy.util import era5_level_pressure, potential_temperature, surface_pressure_hypsometric
from calc_bulk_and_ec_fluxes import load_era5_sl, load_modis, load_obs  # noqa: E402

fs.apply()

# ── colours: one per data source, from the flux palette ─────────────────────
C_OBS = fs.C["H_obs_bulk"]     # KT-19 / T-Bird / Polar 6
C_MOD = fs.C["H_rs_bulk"]      # MODIS T_s on the ERA5 column
C_ERA = fs.C["H_era_diag"]     # ERA5
C_CAR = fs.C["H_car_diag"]     # CARRA

_CARRA = REPO / "data" / "reanalysis" / "carra"
_ERA5_ML = REPO / "data" / "reanalysis" / "era5" / "ERA5_model_levels" / "era5_ml.nc"
_POLAR6_LEVEL = REPO / "data" / "observations" / "ar" / "polar6_level_at_segments.nc"

# ERA5 model levels closest to the surface and their standard-atmosphere heights [m]
# (ECMWF L137 definitions); the level pressure is fluxpy.util.era5_level_pressure,
# as in the reanalysis-driven bulk fluxes.
ERA5_LEVELS = {137: 10.0, 136: 31.0, 135: 54.0, 134: 79.0}
CARRA_LEVELS_M = (30.0, 75.0)

# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Data: the 91 segments and every source colocated to them
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
obs = load_obs()
start_times = pd.DatetimeIndex(obs["start_time"].values)
flight_days = sorted(set(start_times.date))
t_seg = xr.DataArray(start_times, dims="leg")
lat_seg = xr.DataArray(np.asarray(obs["latitude"]), dims="leg")
lon_seg = xr.DataArray(np.asarray(obs["longitude"]), dims="leg")

# observations: KT-19 surface (surface pressure reconstructed hydrostatically from the
# T-Bird pressure, as in the in-situ bulk flux), T-Bird level, Polar 6 level from the
# aircraft-level side file
T_kt19 = np.asarray(obs["t_kt19"], dtype=float)
T_tbird = np.asarray(obs["T_mean"], dtype=float)
p_tbird = np.asarray(obs["p_mean"], dtype=float)
z_tbird = np.asarray(obs["altitude"], dtype=float)
p_sfc_obs = surface_pressure_hypsometric(p_tbird, z_tbird, T_mean=0.5 * (T_kt19 + T_tbird))
theta_sfc_obs = potential_temperature(T_kt19, p_sfc_obs)
theta_tbird = potential_temperature(T_tbird, p_tbird)
polar6 = xr.open_dataset(_POLAR6_LEVEL).reindex(start_time=obs["start_time"].values)
theta_polar6 = np.asarray(polar6["theta_polar6"], dtype=float)
z_polar6 = np.asarray(polar6["z_polar6"], dtype=float)

# ERA5: skin temperature and surface pressure, model levels 134-137; MODIS T_s gap-filled with ERA5 skt
era5_sl = load_era5_sl(obs)
p_sfc_hPa = era5_sl["sp_Pa"] / 100.0
theta_sfc_era5 = potential_temperature(era5_sl["skt_K"], p_sfc_hPa)
ist = np.asarray(load_modis(obs)["IST"], dtype=float)
ist = np.where(np.isnan(ist), era5_sl["skt_K"], ist)
theta_sfc_modis = potential_temperature(ist, p_sfc_hPa)
era5_ml = xr.open_dataset(_ERA5_ML).sel(time=t_seg, latitude=lat_seg, longitude=lon_seg, method="nearest")
theta_era5 = {level: potential_temperature(era5_ml["t"].sel(model_level=level).values,
                                           era5_level_pressure(era5_sl["sp_Pa"], level))
              for level in ERA5_LEVELS}


def load_carra(ds_obs: xr.Dataset) -> dict:
    """CARRA skin temperature and surface pressure, and T and p at 30 and 75 m, at the segments."""
    surface = xr.open_dataset(_CARRA / "carra_east_latlon0p05.nc")[["skt", "sp"]]
    surface = surface.sel(time=t_seg, lat=lat_seg, lon=lon_seg, method="nearest")
    levels = xr.open_dataset(_CARRA / "height_level" / "carra_latlon0p05.nc")[["t", "pres"]]
    levels = levels.sel(valid_time=t_seg, lat=lat_seg, lon=lon_seg, method="nearest")
    out = {"skt_K": surface["skt"].values.astype(float), "sp_Pa": surface["sp"].values.astype(float)}
    for z in CARRA_LEVELS_M:
        at_z = levels.sel(heightAboveGround=z)
        out[f"T{z:.0f}_K"] = at_z["t"].values.astype(float)
        out[f"p{z:.0f}_Pa"] = at_z["pres"].values.astype(float)
    return out


carra = load_carra(obs)
theta_sfc_carra = potential_temperature(carra["skt_K"], carra["sp_Pa"] / 100.0)
theta_carra = {z: potential_temperature(carra[f"T{z:.0f}_K"], carra[f"p{z:.0f}_Pa"] / 100.0) for z in CARRA_LEVELS_M}

# series of panels (b) and (c): surface temperature [degC] and stratification theta(~30 m) - theta_s [K]
T_sfc_series = [(T_kt19, C_OBS), (ist - 273.15, C_MOD), (era5_sl["skt_K"] - 273.15, C_ERA), (carra["skt_K"] - 273.15, C_CAR)]
dtheta_series = [(theta_tbird - theta_sfc_obs, C_OBS),
                 (theta_era5[136] - theta_sfc_modis, C_MOD),
                 (theta_era5[136] - theta_sfc_era5, C_ERA),
                 (theta_carra[30.0] - theta_sfc_carra, C_CAR)]

# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Figure: four profile columns (a) on top, the two histograms (b), (c) below
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
fig = fs.gridfig(width=fs.COL_W, aspect=1.75)
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 4, height_ratios=[2.1, 1, 1])
axs_prof = []
for i in range(4):
    axs_prof.append(fig.add_subplot(gs[0, i], sharey=axs_prof[0] if i else None))
ax_tsfc = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, :])
ax_dtheta = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, :])

# ── (a) profiles ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Y_TOP = 100
valid = ((z_polar6 > 0) & (z_polar6 < 200) & (z_tbird > 0) & (z_tbird < 200)
         & np.isfinite(theta_sfc_obs) & np.isfinite(theta_tbird) & np.isfinite(theta_polar6))
z_tbird_mean, z_polar6_mean = np.nanmean(z_tbird[valid]), np.nanmean(z_polar6[valid])

# (colour, theta at the levels, heights of the levels (per segment or fixed), marker,
#  line style of single segments, line style of the median)
Z_ERA5 = [0.0] + [ERA5_LEVELS[k] for k in (137, 136, 135, 134)]
sources = [
    (C_OBS, [theta_sfc_obs, theta_tbird, theta_polar6], [np.zeros_like(z_tbird), z_tbird, z_polar6], "o", "-", "--"),
    (C_ERA, [theta_sfc_era5] + [theta_era5[k] for k in (137, 136, 135, 134)], Z_ERA5, "^", "-", "--"),
    (C_MOD, [theta_sfc_modis, theta_era5[136]], [0.0, ERA5_LEVELS[136]], "^", ":", ":"),
    (C_CAR, [theta_sfc_carra, theta_carra[30.0], theta_carra[75.0]], [0.0, 30.0, 75.0], "s", "-", "--"),
]
X_LIMITS = [(240, 255), (240, 260), (245, 260), (265, 275)]

for i_day, (ax, day) in enumerate(zip(axs_prof, flight_days)):
    ax.axhline(z_tbird_mean, color="0.75", lw=0.6, ls="--", zorder=0)
    ax.axhline(z_polar6_mean, color="0.75", lw=0.6, ls="--", zorder=0)
    of_day = valid & (start_times.date == day)
    for colour, thetas, heights, marker, ls_single, ls_median in sources:
        per_segment = isinstance(heights[0], np.ndarray)
        for j in np.where(of_day)[0]:                                   # single segments
            z_j = [z[j] for z in heights] if per_segment else heights
            ax.plot([th[j] for th in thetas], z_j, color=colour, lw=0.5, ls=ls_single, alpha=0.1, zorder=1)
        theta_median = [np.nanmedian(th[of_day]) for th in thetas]        # daily median profile
        z_median = [np.nanmedian(z[of_day]) for z in heights] if per_segment else heights
        ax.plot(theta_median, z_median, marker=marker, color=colour, lw=1.6, ls=ls_median, alpha=0.9,
                markeredgewidth=0.25, markeredgecolor="0.3", markerfacecolor=colour, zorder=4)

    x0, x1 = X_LIMITS[i_day]
    ax.set_ylim(-10, Y_TOP)
    ax.set_yticks([0, 50, 100])                                           # sparse: the instrument-level
    ax.set_yticks(np.arange(0, Y_TOP + 1, 10), minor=True)                # labels sit between the ticks
    ax.set_xlim(x0, x1)
    ax.set_xlabel(r"$\theta$ (K)")
    ax.set_title(pd.Timestamp(day).strftime("%d %b"), fontweight="bold")
    major = np.arange(x0, x1 + 1, 10)                                     # labelled every 10 K, minor every 5 K
    ax.set_xticks(major)
    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(x0, x1 + 1, 5), minor=True)
    not_last = i_day < 3                                                  # blank the label on a shared column edge
    ax.set_xticklabels(["" if (not_last and t == x1) else f"{t:.0f}" for t in major])
    if i_day > 0:
        ax.tick_params(axis="y", which="both", left=False, labelleft=False)

axs_prof[0].set_ylabel("Height (m)", labelpad=15)   # clear of the 'T-Bird' / 'Polar 6' labels
fig.legend(handles=[Line2D([0], [0], color=c, lw=1.6, label=name)
                    for c, name in [(C_OBS, "Observations"), (C_MOD, "ERA5–MODIS"), (C_ERA, "ERA5"),
                                    (C_CAR, "CARRA")]],
           loc="outside upper center", ncol=2, columnspacing=1.5, handlelength=1.4, handletextpad=0.4)


def panel_label(ax, label):
    """Panel letter raised above the axes top, clear of the uppermost y tick label
    (local variant of fs.panel_label, whose fixed 2 % offset lets it touch the tick label)."""
    ax.annotate(label, xy=(0, 1), xycoords="axes fraction", xytext=(-4, 7), textcoords="offset points",
                fontweight="bold", ha="right", va="bottom")


panel_label(axs_prof[0], "(a)")
for z, text in [(z_tbird_mean, "T-Bird"), (z_polar6_mean, "Polar 6")]:   # instrument levels, in the
    axs_prof[0].annotate(text, xy=(0, z), xycoords=axs_prof[0].get_yaxis_transform(),   # tick-label
                         xytext=(-5, 0), textcoords="offset points", va="center", ha="right",   # column,
                         color="0.5", fontsize=fs.FONT_SIZE - 1, zorder=5)                  # between ticks

# ── (b), (c) histograms ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step = dict(density=True, histtype="step", linewidth=1.0, alpha=0.9, zorder=2)   # outlines only, no fill
panels = [
    (ax_tsfc, T_sfc_series, np.linspace(-35, 5, 20), (-35, 5), [-1.8, -20],
     [(-1.8, 5, "#fffde7"), (-20, -1.8, "#e3f2fd"), (-35, -20, "#e8eaf6")],
     [(-27.5, "snow-covered\nsea ice"), (-10.9, "thin\nsea ice"), (1.6, "open\nwater")],
     r"$T_\mathrm{s}$ (°C)", "(b)"),
    (ax_dtheta, dtheta_series, np.linspace(-6, 6, 20), (-8, 8), [0],
     [(-8, 0, "#fff3e0"), (0, 8, "#e8eaf6")],
     [(-4, "unstable\nstratification"), (4, "stable\nstratification")],
     r"$\theta_\mathrm{air} - \theta_\mathrm{s}$ (K)", "(c)"),
]
for ax, series, bins, xlim, vlines, bands, labels, xlabel, letter in panels:

    ok = np.isfinite(lats) & np.isfinite(lons)
    tx, ty = _TO_3413.transform(lons[ok], lats[ok])
    return tx, ty, rad.time.values[ok]


def _square_extent(window, min_km, pad_km=15, pad_frac=0.08):
    tx, ty, _ = _track_xy(window)
    pad = pad_km * 1000
    xmin, xmax = tx.min() - pad, tx.max() + pad
    ymin, ymax = ty.min() - pad, ty.max() + pad
    side = max(xmax - xmin, ymax - ymin, min_km * 1000) * (1 + pad_frac)
    xc, yc = 0.5 * (xmin + xmax), 0.5 * (ymin + ymax)
    return xc - side / 2, xc + side / 2, yc - side / 2, yc + side / 2


def _add_scalebar(ax, length_km=50, pad_frac=0.05):
    xl, yl = ax.get_xlim(), ax.get_ylim()
    xspan, yspan = xl[1] - xl[0], yl[1] - yl[0]
    bar_m = length_km * 1000
    if bar_m > 0.45 * xspan:
        bar_m = round(0.30 * xspan / 1e4) * 1e4
        length_km = max(int(bar_m / 1000), 10)
    x0 = xl[0] + pad_frac * xspan
    y0 = yl[0] + pad_frac * yspan
    ax.plot([x0, x0 + bar_m], [y0, y0], "-", color="k", lw=1.5, solid_capstyle="butt", zorder=20)
    ax.text(x0 + bar_m / 2, y0 + 0.03 * yspan, f"{length_km} km", ha="center", va="bottom",
            fontsize=fs.FONT_SIZE - 1, color="k", zorder=20)


def _draw_track(ax, window, zorder=10):
    tx, ty, tt = _track_xy(window)
    if len(tx) < 2:
        return
    ax.plot(tx, ty, color="white", lw=2.2, zorder=zorder - 1, solid_capstyle="round", rasterized=True)
    ax.plot(tx, ty, color=fs.GREY, lw=0.8, zorder=zorder - 1, solid_capstyle="round", rasterized=True)

    day_mask = starts.normalize() == pd.Timestamp(window[0]).normalize()
    d_starts, d_ends, d_ec = starts[day_mask], end_times[day_mask], H_obs_ec[day_mask]
    tw0, tw1 = np.datetime64(pd.Timestamp(window[0])), np.datetime64(pd.Timestamp(window[1]))
    for i in range(len(d_starts)):
        t0 = d_starts[i].to_datetime64()
        t1 = t0 + np.timedelta64(5, "m") if np.isnat(d_ends[i]) else d_ends[i]
        if t1 < tw0 or t0 > tw1:
            continue
        seg = (tt >= t0) & (tt <= t1)
        if seg.sum() < 2:
            continue
        ax.scatter(tx[seg], ty[seg], color=CMAP_TRACK(FLUX_NORM(float(d_ec[i]))), s=3.2, zorder=zorder)


def _gibs_wms_url(layer, extent, date_string, width=1200, height=1200):
    params = {
        "SERVICE": "WMS", "REQUEST": "GetMap", "VERSION": "1.3.0", "LAYERS": layer,
        "CRS": "EPSG:3413", "BBOX": f"{extent[0]},{extent[2]},{extent[1]},{extent[3]}",
        "WIDTH": str(width), "HEIGHT": str(height), "FORMAT": "image/png", "TIME": date_string,
    }
    return "https://gibs.earthdata.nasa.gov/wms/epsg3413/best/wms.cgi?" + urlencode(params)


def _load_cached_png(cache_path, url):
    if not cache_path.exists():
        urlretrieve(url, cache_path)
    return plt.imread(cache_path)


def _extract_legend_ramp(legend_img):
    """Longest coloured pixel run per row of the published legend PNG -> RGB ramp."""
    legend_rgb = np.asarray(legend_img, dtype=float)[..., :3]
    mask = np.any(np.abs(legend_rgb - 1.0) > 0.02, axis=2)
    runs = []
    for row in range(legend_rgb.shape[0]):
        cols = np.where(mask[row])[0]
        if len(cols) < 60:
            continue
        splits = np.where(np.diff(cols) > 1)[0]
        starts_, ends_ = np.r_[0, splits + 1], np.r_[splits, len(cols) - 1]
        c0, c1 = max(((int(cols[s]), int(cols[e])) for s, e in zip(starts_, ends_)),
                     key=lambda item: item[1] - item[0])
        runs.append((row, c0, c1, c1 - c0 + 1))
    if not runs:
        raise RuntimeError("Could not isolate the MODIS IST legend ramp.")
    best_row, best_c0, best_c1, best_len = max(runs, key=lambda item: item[3])
    ramp_rows = [row for row, c0, c1, n in runs
                 if n >= 0.98 * best_len and abs(c0 - best_c0) <= 2 and abs(c1 - best_c1) <= 2]
    return legend_rgb[ramp_rows, best_c0:best_c1 + 1].mean(axis=0)


def _remap_gibs_ist(image, legend_ramp):
    """GIBS serves IST as a pre-coloured PNG; remap it through the published legend."""
    arr = np.asarray(image, dtype=float)
    out = np.array(arr, copy=True)
    if arr.ndim != 3 or arr.shape[2] < 3:
        return out
    alpha = arr[..., 3] if arr.shape[2] > 3 else np.ones(arr.shape[:2], dtype=float)
    preserve = np.all(arr[..., :3] > 0.985, axis=2)
    valid = (alpha > 0) & (~preserve)
    if not np.any(valid):
        return out
    rgb8 = np.clip(np.round(arr[..., :3] * 255.0), 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    unique_rgb, inverse = np.unique(rgb8[valid].reshape(-1, 3), axis=0, return_inverse=True)
    ramp8 = np.clip(np.round(legend_ramp * 255.0), 0, 255).astype(np.int32)
    dist2 = np.sum((unique_rgb.astype(np.int32)[:, None, :] - ramp8[None, :, :]) ** 2, axis=2)
    idx = np.argmin(dist2, axis=1)
    source_temps = np.linspace(*GIBS_IST_SOURCE_RANGE_K, legend_ramp.shape[0])
    mapped = CMAP_IST(IST_NORM(source_temps[idx]))[:, :3]
    flat_rgb = out[..., :3].reshape(-1, 3)
    flat_rgb[valid.reshape(-1)] = mapped[inverse]
    out[..., :3] = flat_rgb.reshape(arr.shape[0], arr.shape[1], 3)
    return out


def _plot_flux_row(ax, window, title, legend=False):
    tw0, tw1 = pd.Timestamp(window[0]), pd.Timestamp(window[1])
    mask = (starts >= tw0) & (starts <= tw1)
    t = mid_times[mask]
    # legend labels = the estimate names of the manuscript's Table 1
    _plot_with_gaps(ax, t, H_obs_bulk[mask], color=fs.C["H_obs_bulk"], lw=1.2, label="T-Bird bulk")
    _plot_with_gaps(ax, t, H_rs_bulk[mask], color=fs.C["H_rs_bulk"], lw=1.2, label="ERA5–MODIS bulk")
    _plot_with_gaps(ax, t, H_era_bulk[mask], color=fs.C["H_era_bulk"], lw=1.2, label="ERA5-only bulk")
    _plot_with_gaps(ax, t, H_era_diag[mask], color=fs.C["H_era_diag"], lw=1.0, ls="--",
                    label="ERA5 model-diagnosed")
    _plot_with_gaps(ax, t, H_car_diag[mask], color=fs.C["H_car_diag"], lw=1.0, ls="--",
                    label="CARRA model-diagnosed")
    _plot_with_gaps(ax, t, H_obs_ec[mask], color=fs.C["H_obs_ec"], lw=1.5, label="EC")
    ax.axhline(0, color=fs.GREY, lw=0.8, ls=":", zorder=1)       # zero line, below the data
    ax.set_ylabel(fs.FLUX_AXIS)
    # Row title above the axes (in-axes titles collide with the 9 pt legend).
    ax.text(0.02, 1.02, title, transform=ax.transAxes, fontweight="bold", va="bottom", ha="left")
    ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%H:%M"))
    ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.MinuteLocator(interval=15))
    ax.xaxis.set_minor_locator(mdates.MinuteLocator(interval=5))
    ax.set_xlim(tw0 - XPAD, tw1 + XPAD)


def _map_panel(ax, image, ext, window):
    ax.imshow(image, extent=ext, origin="upper", zorder=1, rasterized=True)
    ax.set_xlim(ext[0], ext[1])
    ax.set_ylim(ext[2], ext[3])
    _draw_track(ax, window)
    ax.set_aspect("equal", adjustable="box")
    _add_scalebar(ax)
    ax.set_xticks([])
    ax.set_yticks([])
    for sp in ax.spines.values():
        sp.set_visible(False)


def _add_colorbar_below(ax, cmap, norm, label, ticks, ticklabels,
                        bounds=(0.0, -0.13, 1.0, 0.055)):
    """Horizontal colour bar under the bottom map of a column, outside the imagery.

    The bar is an inset of the map axes placed below it (axes coordinates of the
    aspect-equal map, so it spans the image width); constrained layout reserves
    the space because inset axes count towards the parent's tight bounding box.
    """
    cax = ax.inset_axes(bounds)
    sm = plt.cm.ScalarMappable(norm=norm, cmap=cmap)
    cbar = ax.figure.colorbar(sm, cax=cax, orientation="horizontal", ticks=ticks)
    cbar.ax.set_xticklabels(ticklabels)
    cbar.ax.tick_params(axis="x", which="major", length=2.0, width=0.5, pad=1.5)
    cbar.ax.tick_params(axis="x", which="minor", length=0)
    cbar.set_label(label, labelpad=1.5)
    cbar.outline.set_linewidth(0.5)


# ── Norms (IST fixed range; EC flux symmetric about 0 at the 97th pctile) ────
IST_NORM = mcolors.Normalize(vmin=IST_RANGE_K[0], vmax=IST_RANGE_K[1], clip=True)
IST_LEGEND_RAMP = _extract_legend_ramp(
    _load_cached_png(CACHE_DIR / "gibs_modis_ist_legend.png", GIBS_IST_LEGEND_URL)
)
_fabs = float(np.nanpercentile(np.abs(H_obs_ec[np.isfinite(H_obs_ec)]), 97))
FLUX_NORM = mcolors.TwoSlopeNorm(vcenter=0, vmin=-_fabs, vmax=_fabs)

# ── Figure: 6 rows x [time series | IST map | true-colour map] ───────────────
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(fs.FULL_W, fs.MAX_H))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(6, 3, width_ratios=[2, 1, 1])
ts_axes = []

for i, row in enumerate(ROWS):
    ax_ts = fig.add_subplot(gs[i, 0])
    ax_ist = fig.add_subplot(gs[i, 1])
    ax_rgb = fig.add_subplot(gs[i, 2])
    ts_axes.append(ax_ts)

    _plot_flux_row(ax_ts, row["window"], row["title"], legend=row["legend"])
    ax_ts.set_xlabel("Time (UTC)" if i == len(ROWS) - 1 else "")
    fs.panel_label(ax_ts, f"({chr(ord('a') + i)})")

    ext = _square_extent(row["window"], row["min_km"])
    date_string = row["window"][0][:10]
    for ax, layer, suffix, letter in (
        (ax_ist, GIBS_IST_LAYER, "ist", chr(ord("g") + i)),
        (ax_rgb, GIBS_RGB_LAYER, "truecolor", chr(ord("m") + i)),
    ):
        img = _load_cached_png(CACHE_DIR / f"gibs_{row['key']}_{suffix}.png",
                               _gibs_wms_url(layer, ext, date_string))
        if suffix == "ist":
            img = _remap_gibs_ist(img, IST_LEGEND_RAMP)
        _map_panel(ax, img, ext, row["window"])
        fs.panel_label(ax, f"({letter})")

    if i == len(ROWS) - 1:      # one shared colour bar per map column, below it
        # (g-l) show the GIBS layer MODIS_Terra_Ice_Surface_Temp_Day, not the
        # MODIS/Aqua L3 T_s,MOD of the analysis -> labelled as what it is
        _add_colorbar_below(ax_ist, CMAP_IST, IST_NORM, "MODIS/Terra IST (K)",
                            ticks=IST_TICKS_K,
                            ticklabels=[f"{t:.0f}" for t in IST_TICKS_K])
        _add_colorbar_below(ax_rgb, CMAP_TRACK, FLUX_NORM, fs.L["H_obs_ec"] + " " + fs.FLUX_UNIT,
                            ticks=[-10, 0, 10],
                            ticklabels=["\N{MINUS SIGN}10", "0", "10"])

fig.align_ylabels(ts_axes)
handles, labels = ts_axes[0].get_legend_handles_labels()
# two rows, read row by row: bulk estimates on top, model-diagnosed and EC below
# (legend columns fill column-major, hence the interleaved order)
ORDER = [0, 3, 1, 4, 2, 5]
fig.legend([handles[k] for k in ORDER], [labels[k] for k in ORDER],
           loc="outside upper center", ncol=3,
           columnspacing=1.5, handlelength=2.0, handletextpad=0.5)
fs.save(fig, "fig05_flux_timeseries")

pixi run python figures_manuscript/fig06_flux_scatter.py

The script writes figures_manuscript/output/fig06_flux_scatter.pdf and .png at the printed width (one column, 8.3 cm); pixi run figures writes all figures. It uses 

fluxpy.figstyle, 

fluxpy.uncertainty.uncertainty_budget.

Source code (figures_manuscript/fig06_flux_scatter.py)"""Fig. 6 (fig:flux_scatter_comparison) -- bulk vs EC, 2x2 (manuscript Sect. 4.1).

(a) H_S,obs,bulk against H_S,obs,EC;
(b) histograms of the EC, T-Bird bulk and ERA5-MODIS bulk fluxes;
(c) H_S,RS,bulk against H_S,obs,EC;
(d) histograms of the EC flux and the reanalysis-driven estimates.

Scatter points are coloured by the bulk Richardson number; the error bars are the
1-sigma uncertainties of Table 2 (fluxpy.uncertainty). The regression slope b,
correlation r and bias are printed for the caption. All fluxes are positive
upward; the model-diagnosed fluxes are already stored with this sign.

Run:  pixi run python figures_manuscript/fig06_flux_scatter.py
"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.colors as mcolors
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import xarray as xr
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
from scipy import stats
from scipy.stats import gaussian_kde

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))
from fluxpy import figstyle as fs  # noqa: E402
from fluxpy.uncertainty import uncertainty_budget  # noqa: E402

fs.apply()

# ── Data: reference-configuration fluxes ─────────────────────────────────────
ds = xr.open_dataset(REPO / "data/model_output/sensitivity_figure_data.nc")
ref = ds.sel(run="GLGS20_ref", dT=0, dU=0)
H = {k: ref[k].values.astype(float)
     for k in ["H_obs_ec", "H_obs_bulk", "H_rs_bulk", "H_era_bulk",
               "H_era_diag", "H_car_diag"]}
RI = ds["Ri_obs"].values.astype(float)
ec = H["H_obs_ec"]
ec_valid = np.isfinite(ec)

# ── 1-sigma uncertainties of Table 2 (same function as the table) ────────────
BUDGET = uncertainty_budget(ds)
SIGMA = {"H_obs_ec": BUDGET["ec_total"], "H_obs_bulk": BUDGET["obs_bulk"], "H_rs_bulk": BUDGET["rs_bulk"]}


def metrics(x, y):
    m = np.isfinite(x) & np.isfinite(y)
    return (float(np.polyfit(x[m], y[m], 1)[0]),
            float(stats.pearsonr(x[m], y[m])[0]),
            float(np.mean(y[m] - x[m])))

# ── Layout (single column: ~3 cm panels — sparse major ticks, minors carry
#    the 10 W m-2 raster; metric annotations reduced to b / r / bias) ─────────
SC_LIM, SC_TICKS = (-15, 40), [0, 20, 40]
HI_LIM, HI_TICKS = (-25, 40), [-20, 0, 20, 40]
HI_BINS = np.arange(-26, 40.1, 2.0)
cmap_ri = plt.cm.coolwarm_r
# diverging, centred on neutral (Ri_b = 0): red = unstable, blue = stable; the
# +-0.5 range resolves both sides (Ri_b spans about -0.7 to +0.6 between the
# 5th and 95th percentiles); values beyond saturate (colour bar extend="both")
RI_LIM = 0.5
norm_ri = mcolors.Normalize(vmin=-RI_LIM, vmax=RI_LIM)

fig, axes = fs.figure(width=fs.COL_W, aspect=1.1, nrows=2, ncols=2)

# ── (a) + (c): scatter vs EC, coloured by Ri_b ───────────────────────────────
for ax, key in [(axes[0, 0], "H_obs_bulk"), (axes[1, 0], "H_rs_bulk")]:
    y = H[key]
    m = np.isfinite(ec) & np.isfinite(y) & np.isfinite(RI)
    ax.errorbar(ec[m], y[m],
                xerr=np.nan_to_num(SIGMA["H_obs_ec"][m]),
                yerr=np.nan_to_num(SIGMA[key][m]),
                fmt="none", ecolor="0.35", elinewidth=0.3, alpha=0.8, zorder=2)
    top = np.argsort(np.abs(RI[m]))          # draw order only: strongest |Ri_b| on top
    ax.scatter(ec[m][top], y[m][top], c=RI[m][top], cmap=cmap_ri, norm=norm_ri,
               s=10, alpha=0.85, linewidths=0, rasterized=True, zorder=3)
    ax.plot(SC_LIM, SC_LIM, color=fs.GREY, lw=0.7, alpha=0.5, zorder=1)
    b, r, bias = metrics(ec, y)
    ax.plot(np.asarray(SC_LIM), np.polyval(np.polyfit(ec[m], y[m], 1), SC_LIM),
            color=fs.C[key], lw=1.2, ls="--", zorder=4)
    # metrics live in the CAPTION at single-column size — print for provenance
    print(f"caption numbers {key}: b={b:.2f}  r={r:.2f}  bias={bias:+.2f} W m-2")
    ax.set_xlim(SC_LIM), ax.set_ylim(SC_LIM)
    # NB no set_box_aspect here: it silently breaks constrained layout (axes
    # overflow the canvas without warning); near-square comes from the figure
    # aspect instead.
    ax.set_xticks(SC_TICKS), ax.set_yticks(SC_TICKS)
    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(-10, 31, 10), minor=True)
    ax.set_yticks(np.arange(-10, 31, 10), minor=True)
    ax.axhline(0, color=fs.GRID, lw=0.4, zorder=0)
    ax.axvline(0, color=fs.GRID, lw=0.4, zorder=0)
    ax.set_ylabel(fs.L[key] + " " + fs.FLUX_UNIT)

axes[0, 0].tick_params(labelbottom=False)
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel(fs.L["H_obs_ec"] + " " + fs.FLUX_UNIT)

cax = axes[0, 0].inset_axes([0.70, 0.07, 0.05, 0.36])   # empty lower-right corner
cb = fig.colorbar(plt.cm.ScalarMappable(cmap=cmap_ri, norm=norm_ri), cax=cax,
                  ticks=[-RI_LIM, 0, RI_LIM], extend="both")
cb.ax.set_yticklabels([f"\N{MINUS SIGN}{RI_LIM:g}", "0", f"{RI_LIM:g}"])
cb.ax.set_title(r"$Ri_\mathrm{b}$", fontsize=fs.FONT_SIZE - 1, pad=2)
cb.ax.tick_params(labelsize=fs.FONT_SIZE - 1, length=2)
cb.outline.set_linewidth(0.5)

# ── (b) + (d): histograms + KDE over the EC-valid segments ───────────────────
def hist_panel(ax, keys):
    xg = np.linspace(*HI_LIM, 500)
    for k in keys:
        v = H[k][ec_valid & np.isfinite(H[k])]
        lbl = fs.L[k] + (f"  (n={len(v)})" if len(v) < int(ec_valid.sum()) else "")
        ax.hist(v, bins=HI_BINS, density=True, histtype="stepfilled",
                alpha=0.12, color=fs.C[k], zorder=1)
        ax.hist(v, bins=HI_BINS, density=True, histtype="step",
                alpha=0.75, color=fs.C[k], lw=0.9, zorder=2)
        kde = gaussian_kde(v, bw_method=0.4)(xg)
        ax.plot(xg, kde, color=fs.C[k], label=lbl,
                lw=1.2 if k == "H_obs_ec" else 0.8,       # EC heavier: the reference
                zorder=12 if k == "H_obs_ec" else 10)
        ax.fill_between(xg, kde, alpha=0.08, color=fs.C[k], zorder=9)
    ax.axvline(0, color="k", lw=0.6, ls=":")
    ax.set_xlim(HI_LIM), ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)
    ax.set_xticks(HI_TICKS)
    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(-25, 36, 5), minor=True)
    ax.set_ylabel("Density")


hist_panel(axes[0, 1], ["H_obs_ec", "H_obs_bulk", "H_rs_bulk"])
hist_panel(axes[1, 1], ["H_obs_ec", "H_era_bulk", "H_era_diag", "H_car_diag"])
# (b) and (d) on the same density scale, so that their peaks compare directly
HI_YMAX = max(axes[0, 1].get_ylim()[1], axes[1, 1].get_ylim()[1])
for ax in (axes[0, 1], axes[1, 1]):
    ax.set_ylim(0, HI_YMAX)
axes[0, 1].tick_params(labelbottom=False)
# short symbol label: the spelled-out one overhangs the canvas under a ~3 cm
# panel (constrained layout ignores xlabel WIDTH, so it would be clipped)
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel(fs.FLUX_AXIS)

# one legend for all series (per-panel legends would cover the ~3 cm panels).
# ncol=2: three math-symbol columns are wider than the 8.3 cm canvas and make
# constrained layout overflow. Column-major fill -> left column = panel (b)
# series, right column = panel (d) series.
_leg = [("H_obs_ec", 2.0), ("H_obs_bulk", 1.6), ("H_rs_bulk", 1.6),
        ("H_era_bulk", 1.6), ("H_era_diag", 1.6), ("H_car_diag", 1.6)]
fig.legend(handles=[Line2D([0], [0], color=fs.C[k], lw=lw, label=fs.L[k])
                    for k, lw in _leg],
           loc="outside upper center", ncol=3, columnspacing=1.2,
           handlelength=1.0, handletextpad=0.3)

for ax, lbl in zip(axes.flat, ["(a)", "(b)", "(c)", "(d)"]):
    fs.panel_label(ax, lbl)

fs.save(fig, "fig06_flux_scatter")

def diag_metrics(key):
    """(slope, r, bias) of a model-diagnosed flux against the EC reference."""
    h = np.asarray(FIG[key])
    m = np.isfinite(h) & np.isfinite(EC)
    return (float(np.polyfit(EC[m], h[m], 1)[0]),
            float(np.corrcoef(EC[m], h[m])[0, 1]),
            float(np.mean(h[m] - EC[m])))


# ("header", text) rows get no tick and a thin separator line above them;
# ("diag", label, var) rows carry ONE dot — the model-diagnosed fluxes do not
# depend on the bulk configuration.
ROWS = [
    ("row", "Reference ($\\alpha_T = 10^{-1}$)", "GLGS20_ref"),
    ("row", "$\\alpha_T = 10^{-2}$ (amplitude-matched)", "GLGS20_ztr1e-02"),
    ("header", "Stability scheme"),

    ("header", "Model-diagnosed"),
    ("diag", "ERA5", "H_era_diag"),
    ("diag", "CARRA$^{*}$", "H_car_diag"),

        for k in ("H_era_diag", "H_car_diag")}

            df.loc[f"{label}_era5only", f"rs_{metric}"])


fig, axes = fs.figure(width=fs.COL_W, aspect=0.95, ncols=3, sharey=True)

for i, entry in enumerate(ROWS):
    ypos[i] = -float(i)

headers = [(ypos[i], e[1]) for i, e in enumerate(ROWS) if e[0] == "header"]

for ax, (metric, xlab, xlim, ticks, ideal) in zip(axes, PANELS):

            ax.plot(DIAG[entry[2]][metric], yy, "o", ms=4.5, color=fs.C[entry[2]],

    ax.set_xlim(xlim)

    ax.set_xlabel(xlab)
    ax.set_ylim(min(ypos.values()) - 0.6, 0.6)

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import xarray as xr
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
from scipy.signal import detrend

from fluxpy import figstyle as fs
from fluxpy.eddy_covariance import band_covariance, band_covariance_random_error
from fluxpy.qc import segment_spectra
from fluxpy.util import add_theta

fs.apply()

# ── Configuration ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FS = 100.0           # sampling frequency [Hz]

# Line styles = CONTENT (detectability classes), not house styling.
STYLES = {
    True:  dict(color=(0.4189584, 0.69487019, 0.79630958), linewidth=0.8, linestyle="-", zorder=1),
    False: dict(color="0.75", linewidth=0.6, linestyle="-", zorder=0),
}

# ── Segments of the paper and their 100 Hz data ──────────────────────────────
FIG = xr.open_dataset(REPO / "data/model_output/sensitivity_figure_data.nc")
SEG = xr.open_dataset(
    REPO / "data/observations/ar/analysis_ready_polar6_turbulent_fluxes_latest_5km.nc"
).sel(start_time=FIG["start_time"].values)
ds_tb = xr.open_dataset(
    REPO / "data/observations/processed/t-bird_unified/noseboom_unified.nc").sortby("time")

list_of_qcs, detectable = [], []
for t0, t1 in zip(SEG["start_time"].values, SEG["end_time"].values):
    data = add_theta(ds_tb.sel(time=slice(t0, t1))).dropna(dim="time", how="any")
    list_of_qcs.append(segment_spectra(w=data["w"].values, theta=data["theta"].values,
                                       u=data["u"].values, v=data["v"].values, fs=FS))
    w, th = detrend(data["w"].values), detrend(data["theta"].values)
    detectable.append(bool(abs(band_covariance(w, th, FS))
                           > 2.0 * band_covariance_random_error(w, th, FS)))
print(f"{len(list_of_qcs)} segments, {sum(detectable)} above twice their random error")


# ── Plot helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def _add_flux_band(ax, f1=0.1, f2=20.0):
    ax.axvspan(f1, f2, color="0.92", zorder=-5)
    ax.axvline(f1, color="k", linestyle="-", linewidth=0.7)
    ax.axvline(f2, color="k", linestyle="-", linewidth=0.7)


def _add_minus53_guides(ax, f, anchor_idx=3):
    fa = f[anchor_idx]
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore"):       # f[0] = 0 -> inf, not drawn
        for k in range(-6, 2):
            ax.loglog(f, 10.0 ** k * (f / fa) ** (-5 / 3),
                      ls="--", color="0.6", linewidth=0.5)


def _plot_lines(ax, x_key, y_key, scale=1.0, only_detectable=False):
    """One line per segment plus the black median over the plotted segments."""
    rows = [(qc, d) for qc, d in zip(list_of_qcs, detectable) if d or not only_detectable]
    n = min(min(len(qc[x_key]), len(qc[y_key])) for qc, _ in rows)
    for qc, d in rows:
        ax.plot(qc[x_key][1:n], qc[y_key][1:n] * scale, **STYLES[d])
    med = np.nanmedian(np.array([qc[y_key][:n] for qc, _ in rows]), axis=0)
    ax.plot(rows[0][0][x_key][1:n], med[1:] * scale, color="k", lw=1.0, zorder=10)


# ── Figure: (a-d) power spectra | (e) f-cospectrum, (f) ogive ────────────────
fig, axs = plt.subplot_mosaic("AABB\nCCDD\nEEFF", figsize=(fs.FULL_W, 15.0 * fs.CM))

for key, p_key, var_label, ylabel, ymin in [
    ("A", "P_theta", r"$\theta$", r"$P_\theta\;(K^2\,s)$",      1e-6),
    ("B", "P_w",     r"$w$",      r"$P_w\;(m^2\,s^{-1})$",      1e-6),
    ("C", "P_u",     r"$u$",      r"$P_u\;(m^2\,s^{-1})$",      1e-5),
    ("D", "P_v",     r"$v$",      r"$P_v\;(m^2\,s^{-1})$",      1e-5),
]:
    ax = axs[key]
    ax.set_xscale("log")
    ax.set_yscale("log")
    ax.set_xlim(1e-2, 100.0)
    ax.set_ylim(ymin, 1e0)
    ax.set_yticks(10.0 ** np.arange(np.log10(ymin), 1))
    _add_flux_band(ax)
    _add_minus53_guides(ax, list_of_qcs[0]["f"])
    _plot_lines(ax, "f", p_key)
    ax.text(0.17, 0.92, var_label, transform=ax.transAxes, fontweight="bold")
    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)

# (e) frequency-weighted cospectrum, plotted x1000, i.e. in 1e-3 m K s-1
ax = axs["E"]
ax.set_xscale("log")
ax.set_xlim(1e-2, 100.0)
_add_flux_band(ax)

ax.set_xlabel("f (Hz)")
ax.set_ylabel(r"$f\,C_{w\theta}\;(10^{-3}\,m\,K\,s^{-1})$")

# (f) normalised ogive, detectable fluxes only
ax = axs["F"]
ax.set_xscale("log")
ax.set_xlim(1e-2, 100.0)
ax.set_ylim(-0.5, 2.0)
_add_flux_band(ax)
ax.axhline(0.0, color="0.3", lw=0.7)
ax.axhline(1.0, color="0.3", lw=0.7)

ax.set_xlabel("f (Hz)")
ax.set_ylabel(r"norm. $O_{w\theta}$")

# they stay clear of the uppermost y tick labels (10^0, 2.0) on its left; local
# variant of fs.panel_label, whose letters sat on those tick labels
for key, lab in zip("ABCDEF", ["(a)", "(b)", "(c)", "(d)", "(e)", "(f)"]):

                      textcoords="offset points", fontweight="bold", ha="left", va="bottom")

axs["E"].legend(
    [Line2D([0], [0], **STYLES[True]), Line2D([0], [0], **STYLES[False]), Line2D([0], [0], color="k", lw=1.0)],
    [r"$|H_\mathrm{S}| > 2\,\sigma_\mathrm{rand}$", r"$|H_\mathrm{S}| \leq 2\,\sigma_\mathrm{rand}$", "median"], loc="lower left")

The surface temperature determines whether a bulk estimate follows the observed variability. Driven by ERA5

AGENTS.md describes how to check a
statement of the paper against the code and lists the conventions of the analysis.

The repository contains the code and a locked Python environment, but no data: the first steps download the
measurements from PANGAEA and every other input from a Zenodo data record (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23729591). A single command
recomputes every data-derived number, table and figure of the paper and compares the numbers with the committed
reference expected_numbers.txt.

Obtain the repository: on GitHub, Code → Download ZIP and unpack, or
git clone https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis.git.

Install 

pixi, which sets up the exact environment of the paper without modifying the rest of
the system. The environment is locked for Windows, Linux and macOS.

Run in a terminal in the repository folder (on Windows, enter cmd in the address bar of the Explorer window):pixi run all

The first run downloads the environment (a few minutes), the published measurements (about 1.5 GB) and the
Zenodo data record (about 0.2 GB); Figures 1, 4 and 5 download map data once. The run stops with an error if
any number differs from the reference.
